name: Anuvik Thota
identity: Production infrastructure engineer (observability, incident response, Kubernetes at Oracle scale) who now builds agentic LLM systems in production.

education.school: Vasavi College of Engineering, Osmania University

experience.summary: PacSun multi-agent app on Claude Enterprise, MCP, CEO briefs.
highlights: Multi-agent retail intelligence app on Claude Enterprise for PacSun executives, with MCP connectors into internal systems so agents pull live context, rank operational issues into one owner-tagged view, and draft CEO briefs.
Agentic scheduling workflow that ranks open issues by urgency and owner and proposes CEO meeting slots with agendas.

experience.summary: 6-LLM Veracity benchmark across 8 trust pillars, Llama 3.3 70B human-in-the-loop annotation.
highlights: Benchmarked 6 frontier LLMs (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Grok, DeepSeek) on Veracity (factual accuracy), with test suites and automated scoring in the lab evaluation platform across 8 trust pillars.
Rubric-based annotation pipeline on Llama 3.3 70B that labels caseworker notes, scores confidence, and routes low-confidence cases to domain experts for human-in-the-loop review.

experience.summary: Python ETL joining eye-tracking and Qualtrics data.
highlights: Python ETL pipelines turning raw eye-tracking and Qualtrics exports into analysis-ready datasets.
Survey instruments with automated response validation that flags incomplete or inattentive submissions.

experience.summary: Multi-agent ERP migration with human-in-the-loop confidence routing and a Databricks feed.
highlights: Multi-agent ERP migration on the Claude API and LangGraph, containerized with Docker for AWS, Azure, and GCP: manual reconciliation down 68% over 10,000+ GL/AP/AR records from Sage X3 to Sage Intacct.

Nightly Databricks feed across AWS, Azure, and GCP workspaces: 17 financial tables and 4.2M rows into Delta Lake with PySpark, partition pruning and incremental merges held full refresh at 22 minutes.

Human-in-the-loop review layer over Sage REST APIs and MCP tool calling: 83% of records auto-approved above a confidence threshold, turnaround from 3 days to 5.5 hours for 12 client entities, each on its own cloud.

experience.summary: Volunteer research: DQN reinforcement learning agent for NFL fourth-down calls over 420K plays.
highlights: DQN agent for NFL fourth-down calls over 420K plays, with reward shaping on expected points added.
Agreement with EPA-optimal calls up from 68% to 74% on held-out 2024 drives; per-run training time down 40% (52 to 31 min) by vectorizing replay-buffer sampling and removing a data-loader stall.

experience.summary: Observability, incident response, and Kubernetes for NSX at Oracle scale.
highlights: Prometheus and Grafana observability for NSX across 37,000+ enterprise tenants, moving alerting from static thresholds to SLOs on CPU, memory, and p99 latency: 47 dashboards and alert rules, 41% fewer false-positive pages.

P1 MTTR from 94 to 26 minutes (72%) with real-time API diagnostics across 1M+ endpoints on high-throughput event streams, auto-tagging root causes on 400 and 500 series failures so on-call starts with runbook context.
NetSuite search P50 page load down 30% (840 to 588 ms) by profiling query plans, restructuring indexes on hot predicates, and rewriting SQL that drove full scans.
CLI toolchain on Jenkins CI/CD with scripted pre-deployment validation, adopted by 4 teams across NSX: release cycles 34% shorter, failed deploys from 11% to 4%.
Containerized NSX services on OCI with Docker and Kubernetes, autoscaling on custom Prometheus metrics instead of CPU alone, holding p99 SLOs at 2x peak load through release surges.

projects.name: ModelScope
projects.summary: LLM inference optimization and eval suite: Llama-3.2-3B and Gemma-2-2B across 8 quantization configs (FP16, INT8, INT4, NF4) on a T4 GPU.
highlights: INT4 at 2299 MB, 62% below FP16, 13.7 tok/s, MMLU within a point of baseline.
Pareto sweep showed INT8 strictly dominated: 53% more memory and 2.1x lower throughput.

projects.name: GNN fraud detection
projects.summary: Heterogeneous IEEE-CIS fraud graph (726K nodes, 19.5M edges) with a HeteroRGCN.
highlights: Neighbor sampling and focal loss on a 3.5% fraud rate.
0.923 ROC-AUC, +0.03 over tuned XGBoost.
